summary: Rare earth refining (not mining) is the key bottleneck; chemical process innovation is the investable angle
summary_extended: Baker argues that the critical bottleneck in rare earth materials is not scarcity of the raw ore but rather the highly polluting and environmentally destructive chemical refining process required to produce usable rare earth elements. He contends that this refining challenge — not mining access — is what constrains supply chains for defense, EVs, and AI-adjacent hardware, and that China's dominance stems largely from its willingness to tolerate the environmental costs of refining. Atreides has made a direct investment in a private company that has developed a novel, cleaner chemical process for rare earth refining, which Baker views as the more investable angle compared to acquiring mining assets. He implies that public market investors seeking exposure to this thesis would need to identify listed companies pursuing similar process innovation, though he does not name any specific public equities. The thesis is explicitly contrarian in that it reframes rare earths as a refining problem rather than a resource scarcity problem.
